content:
priya: heads up — found repeated KMS-wrapped credential blobs in a partner S3 bucket logs. not sure if exfil or old backups. posting snippets.
priya: log: \n```
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z GET /partner-backups/2026-03-19/creds.enc 200 - user:svc-partner-sync agent:okHttp
metadata: kms_key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/wrap-key-01, ciphertext_size=4096
```
matt: which key id? that path looks like our wrap-key-01. if it’s real ciphertext we need to assume unwrap possible for any credential holder with key access.
sam: agree. immediate steps: 1) snapshot all accesses (audit replay), 2) revoke any Vault leases that might map to those ciphertexts, 3) temporarily restrict key usage (key denylist) while we triage.
jen: +1. also want to know whether partner bucket is allowed to have these blobs — any sync job for backups? @priya do we know job owner?
priya: it’s from partner-sync lambda (aws account 55555). Owner appears to be @alice on infra side. pinging now.
alice: yep that lambda uploads backups. it was supposed to write encrypted metadata only, not full KMS-wrapped creds. investigating.
security-bot: incident created: #inc-523412 (severity: medium) — runbook: kms-leak-template.automations: audit-replay, key-block, lease-revoke.
oncall: assigning oncall to watch for fallout during key operations.
priya: quick triage notes: 1) ciphertexts found across three dates (03-17..03-19). 2) ciphertext size consistent with serialized Vault wrapped blob (saw same pattern in staging). 3) no immediate 3rd-party accesses in IAM logs beyond partner lambda.
matt: can we query Vault to map ciphertext -> lease? run:
```
vault operator rewrap -ciphertext-file /tmp/ct.txt --dry-run
# or list leases: vault list sys/leases/lookup
```
sam: careful with rewrap. dry-run only. real rewrap/unwrap requires key access and will rotate wrapping metadata. prefer to revoke leases by lookup:
```
vault list sys/leases/lookup | grep partner-sync
vault lease revoke -prefix <prefix>
```
jen: RBAC change proposal: temporarily remove kms.cryptoKeys.decrypt on wrap-key-01 from the partner service account, add a short allow for a boxed incident account for controlled unwraps. also flip audit logging to export to long-retention bucket for forensics.
priya: noted. I'll open a minimal RBAC change PR for GCP: remove roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter from svc-partner-sync@55555 and add roles to incident-unwrap@redwood. ETA 30m.
alice: confirm I can coordinate partner-side rollback to stop new uploads. telling them to pause bucket writes and rotate their local backup job.
security-bot: Audit logs archived: gs://redwood-sec-audit/523412/tarball.gz
priya: action items (short):
- priya: run vault lease query + revoke prefix (ETA 20m)
- matt: prepare key denylist patch (GCP IAM) and PR for temporary deny (ETA 30m)
- sam: stand up ephemeral incident-unwrap account and service key, lock it to our incident window (ETA 30m)
- jen: enable export of CloudAuditLogs -> sec-bucket (ETA 45m)
- alice: confirm partner paused uploads + provide list of uploaded object keys (ETA 15m)

sam: also recommend we run an index across S3 for any ciphertext pattern: `grep -a "kms_key=projects/redwood"` and copy matches to forensics bucket.
matt: once denylist in place we should run a controlled unwrap using incident-unwrap account to see plaintext shape — on an isolated host with no network egress. evidence chain only.
priya: will also flag any Vault token with long TTLs in last 7d and revoke if associated with partner-sync paths.
oncall: if anyone needs escalation to legal/partner-relations ping me.
alice: partner confirmed paused. provided object list in DM.
jen: small note — when we change KMS IAM, Cloud KMS may still allow cached keys briefly; plan for a 5-10m drift window and coordinate with oncall for extra monitoring.
priya: logging final — will post follow-ups here after lease revoke and RBAC change. thanks all :thumbsup:
